title: Client-controlled basket cookie is deserialized with pickle
description: The basket cookie is entirely controlled by the client, but it is passed to pickle.loads(). A crafted cookie can execute arbitrary Python code in the web application's process when any basket endpoint reads it.
evidence: read_basket() obtains request.cookies['basket'] at line 16 and calls pickle.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(raw)) at line 20 without authentication or signing; show_basket() calls read_basket() at line 46.

title: Authentication failures are swallowed and protected handlers still execute
description: require_auth catches the abort(401) raised for an unauthenticated request and then invokes the wrapped handler anyway. This defeats the authentication decorator; for example, the gift-card balance endpoint can be called without credentials and returns card balances. Other protected handlers may run with g.user unset and expose error behavior.
evidence: Lines 52-54 call abort(401) when g.user is None, but the broad except at lines 55-58 catches that exception, sets g.user to None, and returns f(*args, **kwargs). The balance endpoint at shopapi/giftcards.py:10-16 is decorated with @require_auth but does not otherwise use g.user.

title: Any authenticated customer can read another customer's order
description: show_order() calls get_order(), which looks up only the supplied order ID and never verifies that the order belongs to the authenticated user. A customer can enumerate order IDs and retrieve other customers' order contents, payment amounts, and refund history.
evidence: show_order() at lines 46-49 returns order_json(get_order(order_id)); get_order() at lines 25-29 queries SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = ? without customer_id, while the ownership check exists separately in own_order() at lines 32-36 but is not used here.

title: Product search concatenates the query directly into SQL
description: The unauthenticated search endpoint inserts the q parameter into a SQL statement without parameter binding or escaping. An attacker can alter the WHERE clause or extract unintended product data.
evidence: Lines 40-42 construct SQL by concatenating q into a LIKE pattern and execute the resulting string.

title: Admin review report is vulnerable to SQL injection through display names
description: The review report interpolates a database-stored display name into SQL. A user can register or change a display name containing SQL syntax, then a staff member viewing the report causes that syntax to be executed. The staff-only gate does not remove the injection risk because the attacker controls the stored value.
evidence: At lines 73-74 customer data is loaded from the user-controlled account record, and line 80 builds `WHERE r.author_name = '{customer['display_name']}'` with an f-string instead of a bound parameter.

title: Review bodies are rendered as trusted HTML
description: Authenticated users can submit arbitrary review text, which is stored and later rendered with the Jinja safe filter. A malicious review can execute JavaScript in every visitor's browser on the product page, including staff or customers who have an active session.
evidence: products.py:82-91 accepts and stores body without HTML sanitization; product.html line 13 renders r.body with `|safe`.

title: Passwords are stored as unsalted fast SHA-256 hashes
description: Passwords are hashed with a single unsalted SHA-256 operation. If the database is exposed, common and reused passwords can be recovered efficiently with precomputed or GPU-based cracking, enabling account takeover.
evidence: hash_password() returns hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest() at lines 15-16; no per-user salt or password-specific KDF is used.

title: Payment status timeouts fail open and mark orders paid
description: When the payment provider request times out, confirm-payment treats the timeout as a successful payment and transitions the order to processing with paid_pence equal to the order total. A provider outage or induced timeout therefore allows fulfillment without confirmed payment.
evidence: The requests.Timeout handler at lines 39-42 sets status = 'paid'; lines 43-45 then set status to processing and paid_pence = total_pence.
